modules.title: 点一下“完成”，页面为什么会变？
一次点击怎样更新页面

items.title: 先听点击，再改画面
items.text: 按钮被点到时，JavaScript 运行为这次点击准备的动作，修改对应的文字或状态，浏览器随即重画这一小块界面。

items.title: 等网络回应，看控制台报错
items.text: 它能向服务器发请求要数据；如果出错了，浏览器控制台（Console）会打印红色报错（如 TypeError: Cannot read property of undefined）。把具体报错发给 AI，比只说“页面坏了”管用得多。

items.title: 认出 AI 写的基本语法
items.text: 不用背全部语法，但认识 const/let（存数据的变量）、function 或 =>（执行动作）、if（条件判断）等词，能帮你大致看懂 AI 写的代码逻辑。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 这页的点击代码运行在浏览器；使用 Node.js 的服务端代码运行在服务器。不要把密码或可信的权限判断只放在浏览器里。

lessonPractice.title: 收藏按钮点击后数字从 4 变成 5，但刷新页面又回到 4。怎样判断问题？

options.label: JavaScript 已更新当前画面，还要确认保存请求和服务器结果是否成功
options.feedback: 浏览器逻辑可以立即改画面，刷新后的结果仍取决于数据是否真正保存。

options.label: 数字已经变化，说明收藏完成，只需阻止页面刷新
options.feedback: 画面变化只是当前浏览器状态，不能证明服务器已经保存收藏。

options.label: 把收藏权限检查全部写进浏览器，服务器直接接受结果
options.feedback: 浏览器代码可被修改，真实权限和数据规则必须由受控服务再次检查。

en.title: A favorite count changes from 4 to 5 after clicking but returns to 4 after refresh. How should the issue be understood?

options.label: JavaScript updated the current view, but the save request and server result still need verification
options.feedback: Browser logic can change the view immediately, while refresh depends on whether the data was persisted.

options.label: The number changed, so saving succeeded and refresh should simply be blocked
options.feedback: A view update is only browser state and does not prove the server stored the favorite.

options.label: Put all favorite permission checks in the browser and let the server accept the result
options.feedback: Browser code can be modified, so real permissions and data rules require a controlled server check.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请检查收藏按钮的 JavaScript：点击后显示保存中，只有请求成功才更新为已收藏，失败要恢复并提示重试。权限和最终数据由服务端校验；用刷新页面验证收藏确实持久保存。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Audit the favorite-button JavaScript: show saving, mark favorited only after success, and restore with retry on failure. Keep permissions and final data validation on the server, then refresh to verify persistence.

learning.assumes: You know a page button can be clicked.
learning.outcome: You can explain how one click can request new data and update what a page shows.

modules.title: Why does one click change a page?
How a click updates the interface

items.title: Handle the click and update the view
items.text: JavaScript runs the action prepared for that button, changes the relevant text or state, and the browser redraws that part of the screen.

items.title: Wait for server results and read console errors
items.text: It can request data over the network. If something goes wrong, the browser Console displays red errors (like TypeError). Copying the exact error to AI is much more effective than just saying 'the page is broken'.

items.title: Recognize basic syntax from AI
items.text: You don't need to memorize all syntax, but recognizing keywords like const/let (variables), function or => (actions), and if (conditions) helps you understand what AI is doing.

modules.title: What people often confuse
modules.text: Browser JavaScript runs on the visitor’s device; Node.js server code runs elsewhere. Do not keep passwords or trusted permission checks only in browser code.
